chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Abī Wallād, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who takes a riding animal and a camel as collateral for his money: does he have the right to ride them? He said: "If he is feeding them, then he has the right to ride them; but if the one who pledged them with him is feeding them, then he does not have the right to ride them."

key_terms.أَرْهَنَهُمَا: pledged the two animals as collateral
key_terms.بِمَالِهِ: for his owed money or financial claim
key_terms.رَهْنًا: collateral or pledge held against a debt
key_terms.يَرْكَبَهُمَا: rides and derives use from the two animals
key_terms.يَعْلِفُهُمَا: feeds and maintains the two animals
key_terms.ٱلدَّابَّةَ: a riding animal taken as collateral

ai.seo_question: Can a creditor ride an animal that has been given as collateral (rahn)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding the use of pledged animals held as collateral. The right to benefit by riding them depends on who bears their maintenance, showing that financial benefit is tied to corresponding responsibility and expense.
